confirmed.title: Gmail compose: Escape, Sift's Close or a click outside hides the draft only in Sift, and it then comes back as a modal sheet over the next email opened
confirmed.evidence: Original: the compose window is a role=dialog box fixed at the bottom right with no close button. Escape and clicks elsewhere leave it open, and the inbox stays usable beside it. Sift shows it as a modal sheet 'New Message' (aria-modal=true, main.inert=true) with its own Close. I typed To 'a@b' and Subject 'Hi', then pressed Escape, clicked Close, or clicked the backdrop at (1100,700). Each time Sift's sheet goes away and focus returns to Compose, but the page's compose is still open with To 'a@b' and Subject 'Hi'. Sift then shows no draft, and nothing is announced. When I then opened 'Your package was delivered', the URL became #inbox/3, and the 'New Message' sheet came back over the email with main.inert=true. I could not read the email, and a click on 'Back to Inbox' did not reach the page (hash stayed #inbox/3). So you cannot read another email while a draft is open, as you can on the original, and closing the sheet does not do what it does on the page. Clicking Sift's Compose again after hiding replaces the draft on this fixture: the fields are empty. Shots: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-5/research/shots/t5r7-gmail-compose-open.png, /home/nico/projects/sift-test-5/research/shots/t5r7-gmail-compose-backdrop.png, /home/nico/projects/sift-test-5/research/shots/t5r7-gmail-compose-returns.png. Caveat: I could not check what Escape does in real Gmail's compose (no sign-in allowed). The modal-versus-floating difference holds whatever Escape does there.
confirmed.repro: cd /home/nico/projects/sift-test-5; SIFT_PORT=9465 SIFT_TAB=x bun scripts/act.ts goto:http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/gmail.html wait:3000 click:Compose wait:1000 press:a press:@ press:b press:Escape wait:1000 "eval:[!!document.querySelector('sift-root').shadowRoot.querySelector('[role=dialog]'), document.querySelector('#compose-root .agP')?.value]" "click:Your package was delivered" wait:1500 "eval:[document.querySelector('sift-root').shadowRoot.querySelector('.sheet')?.getAttribute('aria-label'), document.querySelector('sift-root').shadowRoot.querySelector('main').inert, location.hash]" prints [false,"a@b"] (Sift's sheet is gone, the page's draft is open), then ["New Message",true,"#inbox/3"] (the sheet is back over the email). Click:Close, or a mouse click outside the sheet, in place of press:Escape gives the same result.
confirmed.suspectedCause: Sift renders every page dialog as a modal sheet with a Close that only hides it in Sift (a dismissed key). The dismissal is reset when the page navigates, so the page's non-modal compose window (role=dialog, fixed, small, no close button of its own) returns as a modal. A compose window, or any small fixed dialog that does not cover the page, might be better shown as a non-modal panel, with Sift's Close not offered when the page has none. Leads: dialogIn() and blocksPage() in src/content/extract/generic.ts, the Dialog sheet in src/content/ui/app.tsx, and the compose form in src/content/adapters/gmail.ts.
confirmed.verdict: I reproduced this on the fixture three times, once each with Escape, Sift's Close and a backdrop click at (1100,700). Each time Sift's 'New Message' sheet goes away, focus returns to Compose, and the page's compose stays open with To 'a@b' (and Subject 'Hi' in the backdrop run). Nothing is announced. When I then opened 'Your package was delivered', the hash became #inbox/3 and the sheet came back with aria-modal and main.inert=true. Focus went into the To field, which still held a@b, so the email could not be read. Screenshot: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-5/research/shots/skeptic-n0-returns.png. With Sift off, the original behaves differently: Escape and a click outside leave the compose floating. Clicking the email row opens #inbox/3 beside it, and the draft keeps a@b. Turning Sift back on shows the modal sheet over that email. The cause is in the code. composeDialog() in src/content/adapters/gmail.ts returns no `ref`, so closeDialog stores an undefined ref in dismissedRefs. The navigation reset in index.ts (about line 2032: `elOf(dismissedRefs.get(k))` is null) then drops the dismissal. Sift's own rule says a dismissed dialog the page still shows stays dismissed, and this breaks it. The same missing ref sends closeDialog's Escape to document.body instead of the compose box. Two limits on scope. First, the fixture has no close control, but real Gmail has 'Save & close', which the adapter's close selector matches in English. On English Gmail, Sift's Close and Escape would click it and close the page's compose, so the 'hidden only in Sift, then returns' part would likely not happen there. The Spanish label ('Guardar y cerrar') is not in that selector; I did not verify this. Second, the modal-versus-floating difference holds on real Gmail too: in Sift you must close the draft before you can read another email, which the original does not require. Medium severity is reasonable for the target fixture.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/adapters/gmail.ts composeDialog(), add `ref: refOf(box)`. The dismissal then survives navigation while the page still shows the box, and closeDialog's Escape reaches the compose box. Better: show the page's floating compose as a non-modal form, either as a block in page.blocks like the inline reply editor() or as a non-modal panel, rather than as page.dialog, so the inbox stays usable beside the draft. Also add the Spanish close labels (e.g. aria-label^='Guardar y cerrar') to the close selector. If only `ref` is added, a dismissed draft is hidden in Sift with no way back, so the non-modal form is the real fix.

confirmed.title: A 'session expired, sign in again to save your changes' modal is hidden when it appears while the reader is idle, and Sign in is then unreachable in Sift
confirmed.where: New fixture http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r7-sessionsave.html (/home/nico/projects/sift/research/fixtures/r7-sessionsave.html); also r4int-latedialog.html#nag. Code: src/content/extract/generic.ts marketingModal() and the MARKETING regex, added in round 6 (~line 5806 of the merged file)
confirmed.evidence: Fresh load, no input, wait 6 s. The page shows its modal 'Your session has expired / Sign in again to save your changes…' with Sign in and ×. Sift shows no sheet and no notice, and no 'Sign in' button exists anywhere in Sift (buttons: Skip to content, Menu, Account, Save draft, Preview, Add a photo, Sift). The user then types and presses Save draft: log 'save blocked', and Sift shows 'Not saved: you are signed out. Sign in again to save.' with no way to sign in short of switching Sift off. ?msg=2 ('Log in again to keep saving your work') is also hidden. The control ?msg=3 ('For your security we ended your session…', which names neither signing in nor saving) is shown as a sheet with Close and Sign in. The pre-round-6 build, run in a scratch Chrome on port 9486, shows all three variants as sheets, and shows the r4int-latedialog #nag dialog ('Subscribed / Sign in to save recipes.'). The merged build hides that one too (no sheet 9-14 s after it opens), so the works line 'latedialog #nag opens Subscribed with Close' no longer holds. Shots: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-6/research/shots/r7t6-session-idle-sift.png and /home/nico/projects/sift-test-6/research/shots/r7t6-session-idle-original.png

confirmed.suspectedCause: MARKETING matches '\b(sign in|log in|…)\b.{0,80}\b(save|saving|…)\b', and 'save' there means storing work, not saving money. marketingModal() then hides any late modal with a Close or × button and no field, unless the user's last action opened it.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on 3 runs. On r7-sessionsave.html with no input, the result after 8 s was {pageModal:true, siftSheet:null}. Sift had no sheet and no notice. Its buttons were 'Skip to content | Menu | Account | Save draft | Preview | Add a photo | Sift', with no Sign in. After typing and pressing Save draft, the log said 'save blocked' and Sift showed 'Not saved: you are signed out. Sign in again to save.' ?msg=2 was also hidden. The control ?msg=3 was shown as a sheet: 'Your session has expired · Close · For your security… · Sign in', with focus on Close. I tested the MARKETING regex in generic.ts directly. It matches 'Sign in again to save' (msg 1), 'Log in again to keep saving' (msg 2) and 'Sign in to save' (#nag). It does not match msg 3. marketingModal() then passes on the × button with aria-label Close and no field. round6-fixes.diff adds both MARKETING and the marketingModal() check (lines 1203-1232). The only difference between the hidden and shown variants is the text the regex matches, so this is a round-6 regression. I did not rebuild the pre-round-6 Chrome. That conclusion rests on the diff and the msg=3 control. latedialog #nag is hidden on the merged build ('dialog opened' in the log, no sheet after 11 s). That part is arguably intended, since a 'Sign in to save recipes' nag the page raised by itself is noise under the spec. The real defect is the session-expired case. There, the hidden modal holds the only way to sign in without leaving the draft, so saving work is blocked in Sift. High is fair. Shot: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-6/research/shots/skeptic-session-idle.png
confirmed.fix: In src/content/extract/generic.ts, tighten MARKETING (~line 5807). 'save/saving' should count only as money ('save money', 'save \d+%', 'save up to', 'save $/€', 'savings'), not as storing work ('save your changes/work/draft/progress'). Also make marketingModal() return false when the dialog text says the session expired, timed out or signed the user out (/session (has )?(expired|timed out)|signed out|logged out|log in again|sign in again/i).

confirmed.title: 'Continue with Google' is removed when its container's class contains 'social' (e.g. social-login), so a social sign-up or sign-in is not possible in Sift
confirmed.where: New fixture http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r7-signup.html (/home/nico/projects/sift/research/fixtures/r7-signup.html). Code: src/content/dom.ts:780, the noise class regex, which includes 'social'
confirmed.evidence:
On r7-signup the original has
. Sift's buttons and links are 'Skip to content | Menu | Log in | Show | terms | Create account | Sift', with no Continue with Google. With ?cls=alt (the same box renamed) Sift shows it. With ?cls=social-login it is gone again. On r4-login, where the same button is not inside a .social box, Sift keeps it. The pre-round-6 build also drops it on r7-signup, so this is not new.
confirmed.repro: cd /home/nico/projects/sift-test-6 && SIFT_PORT=9466 SIFT_TAB=T6-fixtures bun scripts/act.ts goto:http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r7-signup.html wait:2500 "eval:[...document.querySelector('sift-root').shadowRoot.querySelectorAll('button,a')].map(b=>b.innerText.trim()).join(' | ')"  then the same with ?cls=alt (it shows) and ?cls=social-login (it is gone).
confirmed.suspectedCause: The class-name noise list treats any 'social' token as share or follow chrome. Sign-in buttons ('Continue with', 'Sign in with', 'Log in with' + provider) should be exempt.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced. On r7-signup.html, Sift's controls are 'Skip to content | Menu | Log in | Show | terms | Create account | Sift'. With ?cls=alt, 'Continue with Google' appears. With ?cls=social-login it is gone. I also tried the real-world class names kc-social-providers (Keycloak) and auth0-lock-social-buttons-container (Auth0). Both drop the button too. Cause: NOISE_TOKEN in src/content/dom.ts:780 includes 'social', and the walker in generic.ts (~line 3334) returns early on any NOISE_TOKEN box outside a dialog. Common identity-provider login pages wrap 'Sign in with Google/GitHub/SSO' in such boxes. An account that only has social or SSO sign-in then cannot sign in or sign up in Sift. This is not a regression, but High is fair.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/extract/generic.ts around line 3334, before dropping a NOISE_TOKEN box: if the token is only 'social', keep the box when it holds a button or link named like /^(continue|sign in|log in|sign up|register) with\b/i or naming a sign-in provider. Keep it also when it sits in a form or section with a password or email field. Alternatively, drop 'social' from NOISE_TOKEN in src/content/dom.ts and rely on SOCIAL_HOSTS and SHARE_LABEL for share and follow bars.

confirmed.title: Date-range calendar: keyboard focus order does not follow where the calendar is drawn
confirmed.evidence: After Enter on Check-in, the calendar is drawn right under the Check-in field (shot /home/nico/projects/sift-test-6/research/shots/r7t6-daterange-open.png). Tab then goes Check-out > Guests > Reserve > Previous month > Next month > November 1, 2026. The original's order is Check-in > Check-out > Previous month > Next month > November 1. A keyboard or screen-reader user passes Guests and Reserve before reaching the dates they just opened. Picking by keyboard works once there (Dec 3 to Dec 5 gives '2 nights × $140 = $280 total'). The pre-round-6 build also places the calendar after the form's controls.
confirmed.repro: cd /home/nico/projects/sift-test-6 && SIFT_PORT=9466 SIFT_TAB=T6-fixtures bun research/r7t6/datekb.ts   (prints the Sift Tab order and the original's DOM order)
confirmed.suspectedCause: The page's non-modal role=dialog calendar is rendered as a popover after the form, outside the form's flow, rather than in place after the date fields.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced, and worse than the claim says. On r5-daterange.html, I pressed Enter on Sift's Check-in, then Tab. The order was Check-out > Guests > Reserve > Previous month > Next month > November 1, 2026. I checked each Tab stop with elementFromPoint inside the shadow root. Check-out (y=342), Guests (y=487) and Reserve (y=595) are all covered by the open calendar sheet: the hits were the calendar's Previous month button, the Mo header and day 2. So for three presses, keyboard focus sits on controls the user cannot see, and only then reaches the calendar. On the original, the calendar comes right after Check-out in the DOM, so the order is Check-in > Check-out > Previous month. Cause: DialogView in src/content/ui/app.tsx draws a field-anchored popup as a fixed '.sheet.suggest' placed under the field, but it sits after main in DOM order. Picking by keyboard still works once there (works.md). This is not a regression. Medium is fair for a keyboard and accessibility product (focus order, and focus hidden behind the sheet).
confirmed.fix: In src/content/ui/app.tsx DialogView, or in index.ts key handling, when a dialog is anchored to a field (anchorOf(d) non-null) and holds focusable controls (a date grid): Tab from the anchor field should move focus to the sheet's first control, and Tab past the sheet's last control should return to the control after the anchor field. Alternatively, render the anchored sheet in the flow right after the anchor field.

confirmed.title: Username availability message is shown but never announced, and Sift's Username field has no description
confirmed.where: New fixture http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r7-signup.html, the Username field (page: aria-describedby='user-hint user-msg', #user-msg aria-live=polite)
confirmed.evidence: After typing 'ana', the page says 'ana is taken. Try ana2026.' in its aria-live=polite region. Sift shows that text as a plain paragraph that is not in any live region, and no Sift live region received any text (__live []). Sift's Username input has aria-invalid=true but no aria-describedby. In Chrome's accessibility tree the textbox is 'Username', description (none), invalid true. A screen-reader user hears 'invalid' with no reason and is never told the name is taken. On the original the message is announced and also describes the field. By contrast, the Email and Confirm password errors are linked by aria-describedby in Sift.
confirmed.suspectedCause: Page live regions under the inert original are not mirrored to Sift's announcer unless they are role=status or alert notices. Also, aria-describedby is carried over only for error paragraphs, not for hint or live-message paragraphs.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced twice, the second time waiting 6 s instead of 1.8 s to give Sift's delayed alert check time. The page's #user-msg (aria-live=polite) said 'ana is taken. Try ana2026.' Sift shows that text as a plain paragraph, not in a live region. Sift's own status region got nothing (__live []). Sift's Username input has aria-invalid=true and aria-describedby=null. In the AX tree it is 'Username | description: (none) | invalid: true', so even the hint '3 to 15 letters or numbers.' is lost. Causes in the code: fieldError() in generic.ts (~line 1715) keeps an aria-describedby target only if it is role=alert or its id or class matches err|invalid|warn ('user-msg'/'hint' do not). newAlert() in index.ts (~line 1501) announces a polite region only within 5 s of an action (actedAt). Typing does not set actedAt; only afterAct() does. So an async validation result while typing is never announced (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages). The original page is inert, so its own live region is not announced either. Medium is fair.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/extract/generic.ts fieldError(): when the field is aria-invalid, also take aria-describedby targets that are aria-live or role=status. Better, also carry the field's full aria-describedby text into the Field (a desc), and render it in app.tsx as the input's aria-describedby. In src/content/index.ts newAlert(): treat a polite region that the field the user is typing in references through aria-describedby (or aria-errormessage) as an answer even without a recent actedAt. Or set actedAt on typing.

confirmed.title: A rewritten or removed paragraph leaves its old fact in the Short version: the old and new death toll show side by side, for good after the refresh limit
confirmed.evidence: Chrome 9469 with the mock, r7ai/fx/rewordlive.html. The lede alternates between 'The death toll … rose to N' and 'Officials now say N people died after rescuers searched…'. With ?at=6000, the Short version at 12 s shows both 'Officials now say 31 people died…' and 'The death toll from the storm rose to 12.'. With ?at=6000&every=17000: at 90 s it shows '107 people died' next to 'rose to 88'. At 115 s it shows '145 people died' next to 'rose to 88'. The call count stayed at 3 from 70 s to 130 s, so the refresh limit had been reached. Offline (r7ai/t/reword.ts): the model's 'The storm killed 12 people.' stays next to the new paragraph 'Thirty-one people are now confirmed dead…'. r7ai/t/removed.ts: when the paragraph 'Police said two men were arrested…' is removed from the article, 'Police arrested two men for looting.' stays in the Short version.
confirmed.repro: bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r7ai/t/reword.ts and t/removed.ts (run from /home/nico/projects/sift-test-9). In Chrome: start r7ai/mock.ts (port 8871), SIFT_PORT=9469 bun r7ai/settings.ts, then SIFT_PORT=9469 SIFT_TAB=R3-ai-background bun r7ai/watch.ts 'rewordlive.html?at=6000&every=17000' 12,30,50,70,90,100,115,130 'toll|died|killed'
confirmed.suspectedCause: staleAbout counts an old paragraph as changed only when a fresh paragraph shares at least half its tokens (dice >= 0.5). It returns null when no paragraph is fresh, and it takes `gone` numbers only from those changed paragraphs. A lede rewritten in other words (common in live news) or a removed paragraph is never treated as stale. After MAX_REFRESH, nothing replaces the old sentence. Fix lead: treat every old paragraph that is no longer in the article as changed, with or without a close replacement. Drop the sentences that best match it, and drop any sentence stating a number it held that the article no longer has.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, high. Offline, t/reword.ts keeps 'The storm killed 12 people.' next to the full new paragraph in both wordings ('Thirty-one people are now confirmed dead…' and 'Officials now say 31 people died…'). t/removed.ts keeps 'Police arrested two men for looting.' after that paragraph is gone, with proseChanged true. In Chrome 9469 with the mock, rewordlive.html?at=6000 showed 'Officials now say 31 people died…' next to 'The death toll from the storm rose to 12.' at 12 s. The refresh fixed it by 20 s. With ?at=6000&every=17000, the condense calls stopped at 3 from 70 s to 140 s (one refresh came from the cache, so all 4 MAX_REFRESH were used). At 90 s it showed '107 people died' next to 'rose to 88', and at 115 s '145 people died' next to 'rose to 88'. When the lede went back to the 'rose to N' wording (100 s, 130 s), staleAbout did drop the old sentence. So only reworded or removed paragraphs are missed, as the claim says. The cause is in the code: staleAbout (short.ts:369-380) returns null when there is no fresh paragraph, and counts an old paragraph as changed only when a fresh one has dice >= 0.5 with it. The gap lasts until the refresh lands, and for good once the limit is reached.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/short.ts staleAbout: drop the `!fresh.size` early return. Count every old paragraph whose fingerprint is no longer in src.dfp (within sentUnits) as changed, with or without a close fresh match. Take `gone` numbers from all of those paragraphs. Keep the best-match test so that sentences mainly about a gone or reworded paragraph are dropped, and keep the restore logic for merged facts. Optionally, in ai.ts once MAX_REFRESH is reached and the prose still differs, show the full text instead.

So do '[новые правила](L0)' for 'новых правил парковки', '[die neue Parkregel](L0)' for 'die neuen Parkregeln', and '[Book an appointment](L0)' for 'click here'. Chrome with the mock, r7ai/fx/linkword.html: the Short version shows 'Book an appointment online…' as plain text. The booking link appears only at the end, as 'Links in the full text: click here'. r7ai/fx/linkmany.html is the same article with 33 distinct links: the booking link is nowhere in the Short version. Before round 6 the link stayed on 'Book an appointment' and opened /book.
confirmed.repro: bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r7ai/t/inflect.ts and t/here2.ts. In Chrome with the mock: SIFT_PORT=9469 SIFT_TAB=R3-ai-background bun r7ai/outline.ts linkword.html 4 (and linkmany.html)
confirmed.suspectedCause: sameWords needs an exact shared token of 4 or more letters, or 2 shared tokens. Inflected forms (nueva/nuevas, правила/правил, Parkregel/Parkregeln) fail. So does a descriptive phrase that replaces a generic label ('click here', 'aquí'). The extra list is skipped when there are more than 30 distinct links. Fix lead: also accept words that share a stem or prefix with Link.a, or that appear in the source sentence around the link. When the words are rejected, keep the link on the source's own words instead of dropping it.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, medium regression from the F616 fix. Offline, t/inflect.ts strips the link from '[la nueva norma](L0)' (source 'las nuevas normas de estacionamiento'), '[новые правила](L0)' ('новых правил парковки'), '[die neue Parkregel](L0)' ('die neuen Parkregeln') and '[Book an appointment](L0)' ('click here'). The link moves to the extra list. Only '[the application form](L0)' for 'this form' keeps it. t/here2.ts, with 33 distinct links: the booking link is nowhere in the plan. In Chrome with the mock, linkword.html showed 'Book an appointment online…' as plain text, plus 'Links in the full text: [link] click here'. linkmany.html showed the same plain text with no extra list, so the link is reachable only after 'Show full text'. sameWords (short.ts:337-349) needs an exact shared token of 4 or more letters, so inflected forms and a descriptive rewrite of a generic label always fail. I did not run a pre-round-6 build. The 'before round 6' behavior comes from F616's own description (no code checked the words then). The prompt does tell the model to keep link words, so how often real models trip this is unmeasured. Inflection changes in Russian and German rewrites, and 'click here' turning into a descriptive phrase, are plausible.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/short.ts sameWords: also accept a match on a shared prefix stem (for example, the first 4-5 letters of tokens of 4 or more letters, so nueva/nuevas and Parkregel/Parkregeln match). Also accept model words that appear in a small window of the source paragraph around that link (the source sentence 'To book an appointment, click here'). Still reject words that match another link's text better, which keeps the F616 protection. In planShort (around :674), always list a link that sameWords rejected in plan.extra, even when distinct.size > 30, so it never vanishes from the Short version.

confirmed.title: A lines batch that stops at a filter or the output limit now keeps the title of every unanswered entry, on the page and for a day: one flagged headline, or a batch in a long-token script, loses the lines of the whole batch
confirmed.evidence: Mock, r7ai/fx/onefilter.html: 6 headlines, one marked [FILTER]. The mock stops the batch with finish_reason content_filter, as a filter or a 403 moderation of the batch input would. After 3 calls (the chain), all 6 keep their titles, and a revisit makes 0 calls. IndexedDB holds keep-title entries with a 1-day TTL. r7ai/fx/limit.html: the mock stops with finish_reason length after the first line. 1 entry gets a line, the other 4 keep their titles, there is 1 call, and a revisit makes 0 calls. The budget does not depend on the script. By the code's own estTokens, a 12-word Tamil line as JSON is 115 tokens and a Hindi one 82 (r7ai/t/budget.ts), so a 25-entry Tamil batch (1,370 tokens) fits about 11 lines. Before round 6, cut entries were asked for again. I could not measure real token counts without paid calls.
confirmed.repro: Mock running and settings set, then: SIFT_PORT=9469 SIFT_TAB=R3-ai-background bun r7ai/watch.ts onefilter.html 5,12 'Police|court|plain line' twice (the second run shows 0 calls), and the same for limit.html. bun r7ai/t/budget.ts for the token estimates.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The F610 fix treats every final error alike. A filter or an output limit is about the batch, not each entry. Fix lead: on 'length', ask once more for the unanswered entries in a smaller batch. On a filter or moderation stop, split the batch to isolate the flagged entry, and cache KEEP_TITLE only for entries that fail alone. Size maxTokens from estTokens of the titles, as condense does.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed as code behavior, medium at most. The regression covers only the output-limit case. In Chrome with the mock, after clearing the cache, onefilter.html made 3 lines calls (the whole chain filtered with no text). All 6 headlines kept their titles at 5 s and 12 s, and a second visit made 0 calls. Control: the same page without [FILTER] gave all 6 'Plain line' rewrites in 1 call. Before I cleared the cache, the control page also sent only the flagged headline, because the 5 innocent headlines were cached KEEP_TITLE site-wide. limit.html: 1 call, 1 line, 4 titles kept, a revisit made 0 calls. idb.ts shows keep-title rows with ttlDays 1. background/index.ts:581 caches KEEP_TITLE for every unanswered entry on any final Incomplete. Caveats: (1) For the filter case, the outcome is not new. Before the F610 fix, the same batch, flagged entry included, was re-sent and filtered again (endlessly), so those entries got no lines then either. Only the length case loses entries that a smaller retry would have answered. (2) A filter with no text moves the chain to the next model.
